newsitem.title: INDIA: India asks Weizman to improve ties with Syria.
newsitem.headline: India asks Weizman to improve ties with Syria.

text.p: India asked visiting Israeli President Ezer Weizman on Monday to improve ties with Israel's neighbouring Arab states, including Syria, Indian Foreign Minister Inder Gujral said.

Gujral said Weizman's response was positive to India's concerns on the faltering Midde East peace talks, and added: "We are equally keen that their relationship with the neighbouring countries, including Syria, should improve."

"Their response was positive. They said they are trying to restore the health of the agreements, the peace process," Gujral told reporters after talks between the two sides headed by Weizman and Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.

In an interview shown by India's Doordarshan television on Saturday, Weizman described Syrian President Hafez Assad as "sulking" with Israel but said that would not hamper the progress of eventual talks with Damsacus.

Earlier on Monday, Weizman told reporters after a ceremonial reception at the Presidential Palace, that talks with the PLO over the stalled Hebron deal were difficult but they had been put back on track.
